data.body:
_More from Khopkar · Miscellaneous systemic drugs_

**Class:** Progestogen with strong anti-androgenic activity (androgen receptor blocker)

## Mechanism of action
- Blocks androgen receptors; as a progestogen suppresses LH → lower ovarian androgen production
- With ethinylestradiol (2 mg + 35 µg) acts as a combined oral contraceptive

## Indications in dermatology & STI
- Acne in women (moderate–severe, not responding to other therapy), hirsutism, PCOS, female pattern hair loss
- High-dose: prostate cancer, paraphilias (men)

## Dose & formulations
- CPA 2 mg + ethinylestradiol 35 µg daily for 21 days, 7-day break
- Severe hirsutism: add CPA 25–100 mg on days 1–10 of cycle (reverse sequential regimen)

## Adverse effects
- Venous thromboembolism (higher than some other COCs)
- Meningioma with long-term high doses (EMA restriction 2020 — use lowest dose, MRI if symptoms)
- Hepatotoxicity at high doses, mood change, weight gain, breast tenderness, loss of libido

## Contraindications
- Pregnancy, thrombosis history, liver disease, meningioma, smokers over 35, migraine with aura

## Drug interactions
- Enzyme inducers (rifampicin, carbamazepine) reduce efficacy

## Monitoring
- BP, weight; LFT at high doses

## Pregnancy & lactation
Contraindicated (feminises male fetus).

## Viva points
- Anti-androgen + contraceptive in one pill
- Meningioma risk with long-term high doses
- Stop 3 cycles after acne clears (VTE risk)

_Sources: Wolverton 4e ch.34; Khopkar (Antiandrogens). Facts summarised in our own words; Wolverton followed where books differ._
